outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Adapting Foundation Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the context of modern deep learning, focusing on the rise of massive foundation models like LLMs and Vision Transformers. It discusses the prohibitive cost of training from scratch and establishes the necessity of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). It reviews existing PEFT strategies—full fine-tuning, adapter tuning, prompt tuning, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA)—highlighting their trade-offs regarding parameter count, computational cost, and inference latency.
subtopics: The Era of Large Foundation Models
Cost Barriers to Training from Scratch
Model Finetuning vs. Adapter Tuning vs. Prompt Tuning

outline.description: This chapter delves into Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), a principled approach that preserves the geometric relationships between neurons during adaptation. It explains the mathematical motivation behind preserving pairwise angles between neurons to maintain semantic knowledge. The chapter details the mechanism of OFT using multiplicative orthogonal matrices rather than additive updates, covering Cayley parameterization and the initial implementation using block-diagonal structures.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Moving beyond standard algebraic views, this chapter introduces a novel conceptual framework: viewing dense orthogonal matrix generation as an 'information transmission' problem on a grid-structured graph. It analyzes how sparse matrix factorization allows information to flow from input nodes to output nodes across multiple layers. This section defines the desiderata for efficient factorization: achieving dense connectivity with minimal trainable edges (parameters) while maintaining orthogonality constraints.
subtopics: Impact of Orthogonality on Edge Topology
